crowdstrike.goal: Recreate a small endpoint-investigation and containment workflow using simulated devices.
crowdstrike.input: DeviceEvent { deviceId, actorId, process, parentProcess, observedAt, sourceVersion }
components: Sensor simulator
Emit ordinary and suspicious process events for two fictional devices. Include one device that becomes unreachable.
Investigation workspace
Group related events into a case without discarding their device IDs or timestamps. Let an analyst record a verdict and the evidence used.
Containment adapter
Accept a permitted action request, return a request ID, and separately record whether the fictional device applied it. Offline means pending, not contained.
crowdstrike.exercise: Send a detection for device A, request containment, then make the adapter accept while A is offline. Bring A back and inspect the difference between accepted, applied and independently checked.
checks: Device A's event is never attached to device B's action.
An offline acceptance does not set containment_verified.
Undo and ordinary device access are checked after the simulated incident.

palo-alto.goal: Recreate a permission-aware response dispatcher with a visible approval boundary.
palo-alto.input: ActionProposal { customerId, assetId, assetType, action, requestedBy, policyRevision }
components: Permission table
Define allowed, approval-required and forbidden actions for workstation and server fixtures. Treat a policy revision as part of the request context.
Approval workflow
Persist the proposal and decision. A denied or waiting proposal never reaches the effect adapter.
Action verifier
Check the target's post-action state and retain rollback information separately from the dispatcher result.
palo-alto.exercise: Propose the same action for a workstation and a server with different configured authority. Change the policy while one proposal waits and require a fresh decision.
checks: Forbidden actions produce no adapter call.
Approval applies to the intended action and current policy context.
A successful adapter return is not itself the verified target state.

fortinet.goal: Recreate an event-to-network-rule workflow with deterministic automation and an optional assistant.
fortinet.input: NetworkEvent { source, destination, ruleId, decision, observedAt, gatewayId }
components: Gateway fixture
Evaluate local synthetic requests against a small rule table. Record the rule revision and observed decision.
Connector dispatcher
Map an explicit case action to a typed gateway operation. Use separate credentials/capabilities for reading events and changing rules.
Assistant boundary
Allow a model or a deterministic stub to summarize evidence. Require an explicit authorized operation before rule changes.
fortinet.exercise: Create a rule that blocks an unwanted synthetic request and confirm a legitimate control remains allowed. Then feed the same event twice and inspect duplicate action handling.
checks: The rule changed on the intended gateway.
Legitimate traffic in the control case still passes.
Assistant text cannot invoke a write outside the dispatcher policy.

microsoft.goal: Recreate a narrow phishing-report investigation with separately authorized follow-up actions.
microsoft.input: ReportedMessage { reportId, tenantId, messageId, reporterId, suppliedSignals }
components: Investigator identity
Grant a fictional investigator access to the supported message/case records only. Keep unrelated tenant and response capabilities unavailable.
Classification workflow
Gather evidence, record a classification and route uncertain or malicious cases to review. Closing an alert changes that alert's state only.
Response adapter
Represent message removal or account changes as separately authorized actions with their own outcome records.
microsoft.exercise: Feed one benign report, one suspicious report and one report with missing required data. Compare closure, escalation and insufficient-evidence states.
checks: Closing an alert does not silently claim all message copies were removed.
Missing inputs do not become a benign classification.
The investigator cannot cross the fixture's tenant boundary.

cisco-splunk.goal: Recreate a source-event-to-detection pipeline, then add capability-limited guided triage.
cisco-splunk.input: SecurityEvent { sourceType, eventType, subject, target, fields, observedAt }
components: Source normalizer
Map an explicit input schema to the fields expected by one detection. Retain unmapped/missing-field states.
Detection registry
Version the query and test data together. Keep raw matched event IDs with the generated alert.
Triage adapter
Expose selected enrichment and response connectors with explicit tool capabilities and batch/daily budgets. Keep feature-specific model requirements separate.
cisco-splunk.exercise: Run a matching event, a near miss and a matching-looking event missing a required field. Then exhaust a small synthetic triage budget and show unprocessed items.
checks: The expected raw events explain each alert.
Skipped or over-budget cases remain visible.
Connector configuration determines allowed effects; a general assistant setting is not reused as a universal triage contract.

google-mandiant.goal: Recreate an asynchronous investigation service and a consultant-style evidence handoff.
google-mandiant.input: InvestigationRequest { caseId, tenantId, alertIds, contextRefs, requestedAt }
components: Job API
Implement submit, status and result retrieval over a local job store. Define capacity rejection and failure rather than assuming every request enters a queue.
Investigation compiler
Collect source-linked observations into a report with open questions, confidence limits and suggested next work.
Separated conversational client
Keep chat settings, investigation execution and consequential actions in different adapters. Settings changes need their own explicit state and audit record.
google-mandiant.exercise: Submit a complete case, an unsupported input and an over-capacity case. For the complete case, follow each report statement back to a retained observation.
checks: A recommendation never silently becomes containment.
Rejected capacity is distinguishable from a queued job.
The report preserves missing evidence instead of manufacturing a complete incident narrative.

trend-micro.goal: Recreate a multi-source investigation with read-only AI exposure and a tracked response task.
trend-micro.input: ResponseTask { taskId, customerId, targetId, action, approvalRef, state }
components: Source adapters
Normalize two fictional product streams while retaining their original IDs and errors.
Tool exposure policy
Publish read tools by default. Maintain a separate allowlist for each write tool and its permitted arguments.
Task tracker
Track requested, queued, applied, failed and verified states. The result payload and the target observation remain separate.
trend-micro.exercise: Ask a read-only assistant for an investigation summary, attempt an unavailable write, then submit an approved response through the action path with a delayed target.
checks: Read-only exposure produces no write-capable call.
A pending task is not counted as enforced protection.
Data sent to an external assistant is separately inventoried from product-internal processing.

lac.goal: Recreate a human-led, multi-customer monitoring operation over more than one supported event platform.
lac.input: Case { customerId, sourcePlatform, evidenceRefs, severity, owner, escalationState }
components: Customer boundary
Separate credentials, event stores and case access. Shared analyst views must still enforce per-customer access.
Platform adapters
Support two explicit SIEM fixture schemas. Preserve collection-health and query failures instead of flattening them into no alerts.
Shift and escalation workflow
Assign case ownership, record handovers and notify the agreed customer contact for decisions outside the operator's mandate.
lac.exercise: Inject a high-severity case while its assigned analyst's shift ends and one source stops delivering. Work through ownership, customer notification and source-health investigation.
checks: The handover leaves a named owner.
Source silence is visible as collection health, not a clean environment.
A report/escalation does not imply the operator changed the customer's systems.

nri-secure.goal: Recreate a phase-gated analyst-assistance workflow with customer-specific procedures.
nri-secure.input: AnalysisContext { customerId, procedureRevision, alertRefs, permittedQueries, reportTemplate }
components: Phase orchestrator
Advance through triage, analysis, severity scoring and report preparation in an explicit order.
Execution and review roles
Have a worker gather observations and a reviewer check each phase's stated requirements. Return for rework when evidence is missing.
Human decision point
Require the configured human decision for important outputs and separate any future response capability from present analysis.
nri-secure.exercise: Provide a case with a missing observation. Make the reviewer request rework, then give both roles the same mistaken input and inspect why agreement is not independent validation.
checks: A phase cannot advance solely because a model wrote “complete.”
Procedure revisions stay attached to the case.
The report does not imply an account was automatically disabled.

gmo-ierae.goal: Recreate a scoped assessment delivery and a separate optional blocking workflow.
gmo-ierae.input: Finding { scopeRef, actor, affectedRule, requestRef, responseRef, consequence, reviewState }
components: Assessment workspace
Track hypotheses separately from reproduced and reviewed findings. Preserve the account and object involved in each test.
Reporting and retest
Explain the business consequence, repair owner and exact repeatable check. Track a new repaired-version observation.
Blocking adapter
If a separate operating exercise includes blocking, require a permitted rule change and verify its effect and false-blocking controls.
gmo-ierae.exercise: Investigate the order-access lab, write one reviewed finding and one unconfirmed hypothesis, then retest the repaired mode. Deliver the blocking exercise as a different service item.
checks: A second opinion remains advice until a change is actually authorized and performed.
A report's closed state is linked to fresh retest evidence.
Legal entities and purchased service scopes remain separate in the deliverable.

gmo-flatt.input: RepairCase { repositoryRevision, targetScopeRef, hypothesis, reproducer, proposedPatch, verificationRefs }
components: Intake and scope
Record which repository and optional running target may be inspected. Repository access does not define every live target's ownership.
Reproduction and patch workspace
Produce a failing check against a known revision before proposing a change. Preserve unconfirmed hypotheses when no reproduction is available.
Independent regression
Run the original check against the repair plus a normal-behavior control. A proposed patch or PR is not the verification result.
gmo-flatt.exercise: Treat vulnerable mode as a known source revision, describe the missing owner check, implement a repair in a separate copy and run the six fixture checks. Review what the test suite still leaves out.
checks: The patch addresses the intended rule, not merely the visible response label.
The normal owner-access control still succeeds.
Benchmark and future deployment claims retain their exact feature, date and test distribution.
